cards.h: How a single cell becomes a person
cards.b: Nine months turn one fertilised cell into a baby with trillions of cells. Understanding reproduction supports health education, family planning and the treatment of infertility, a matter that affects millions of couples in India.

Sperm (male) and eggs (female) are haploid cells made by meiosis. Sperm are made in the testes and travel through the epididymis and vas deferens. Eggs mature in the ovaries; a girl is born with about a million immature eggs and typically about 400 are released in life.

About 28 days, controlled by hormones.

  1. Days 1-5: menstruation (the lining sheds).
  2. FSH grows a follicle; oestrogen rebuilds the lining.
  3. Day 14: an LH surge causes ovulation.
  4. Progesterone from the corpus luteum prepares the uterus.
  5. If no pregnancy, hormone levels fall and the cycle restarts.
The sperm meets the egg in the fallopian tube. Fusion makes a zygote (2n). It divides (cleavage) into a ball of cells, the blastocyst, which implants in the uterine wall at about day 6-7.

The placenta passes oxygen and nutrients from mother to foetus and waste back, without mixing the bloods. It also makes hormones (hCG, which pregnancy tests detect). Pregnancy lasts about 38 weeks from fertilisation. Organs form in the first 8 weeks, the most sensitive period for drugs and viruses.
Oxytocin triggers contractions. After birth, prolactin makes milk and oxytocin lets it flow. Early breast milk (colostrum) is rich in antibodies.

Methods include barriers (condoms), hormonal pills, copper-T, and sterilisation. In vitro fertilisation (IVF) makes an embryo outside the body; the first IVF baby, Louise Brown, was born in 1978 (Robert Edwards, Nobel 2010).

Karl Ernst von Baer found the mammalian egg (1827). Hans Spemann and Hilde Mangold (1924) showed an 'organiser' region guides the embryo. Hox genes explain body layout. Sex is set by the Y chromosome gene SRY (1990).

Fix these

  • The father's sperm decides the baby's sex (X or Y), not the mother.
  • Ovulation does not always occur on day 14.
  • The placenta is a filter, not a wall: some viruses and drugs cross.

Dr Subhash Mukhopadhyay performed India's first IVF birth (Durga, Kolkata, 1978), only months after Louise Brown, but his work was not recognised during his lifetime. Dr T.C. Anand Kumar delivered India's first officially recorded IVF baby in 1986. India's total fertility rate dropped to about 2.0, under replacement level, per NFHS-5 (2019-21). Janani Suraksha Yojana (2005) promotes safe institutional births.

• Gametes are haploid and made by meiosis.
  • Cycle: FSH, oestrogen, LH surge, progesterone.
  • Fertilisation, implantation, placenta, birth.
  • IVF began in 1978.
